newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy wants Berisha to go but not now - dep minister.
newsitem.headline: Italy wants Berisha to go but not now - dep minister.

text.p: Italy believes Albanian President Sali Berisha should leave office but will not push for his resignation now, deputy foreign minister Piero Fassino said on Tuesday.

Fassino's remarks were the first open indication that Italy, preparing to lead a multinational security force into Albania to assist in the delivery of relief aid, had withdrawn all support from the embattled rightist president.
Fassino, whose area of responsibility includes the Balkans, made his remarks to a leadership meeting of the Democratic Party of the Left (PDS), the biggest party in Italy's government.
"That Berisha should go is very clear, at least to us. And when I say us I'm not just talking about the PDS, I'm also talking about the government," Fassino said.
But he said that if Berisha were to leave office now, his departure would threaten the survival of Albania's national unity government, led by opposition Socialist Bashkim Fino.

Berisha agreed to set up the broad-based government last month pending early general elections after armed anarchy erupted in Albania. Rebel committees in control of towns in the south are demanding Berisha's resignation.
